Consumer spending rose a solid 3.2%, but net trade subtracted 1.0pp (tariff-driven import strength) and inventory drawdowns cut a further 0.7pp. Released the day before China's Politburo meeting and a week before the weak July jobs report — part of a broader mixed-growth-signal window.

label: US Unemployment Rate
deltaNote: July 2026 (Aug 7): NFP fell 23,000 — a sharp miss vs the ~83,000 gain expected — with May and June revised down a combined 103,000. Unemployment eased to 4.1%, largely on lower labor-force participation rather than underlying strength. Markets read the report as reducing Fed hike risk; S&P 500 closed at a record high same day.

label: US PCE Inflation (May 2026 — Highest Since 2023)
deltaNote: MAY 2026 (released June 25): Headline PCE 4.1% YoY (+0.4% MoM) — highest since April 2023. Core PCE 3.4% YoY (vs 3.3% forecast). Personal income and spending each +0.7% MoM; saving rate held at 3%. Released just over a week after Warsh's hawkish dot plot, complicating the disinflation narrative even as Iran-deal oil relief began working through the data. June CPI (July 14) subsequently cooled to 3.5%, suggesting May PCE may mark the cycle high.

label: Fed Funds Rate
source: Federal Reserve FOMC, July 29 2026 (held; 3 hawkish dissents)
delta: Held at 3.50-3.75%; 3 dissents wanted a hike
deltaNote: July 28-29: FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% despite the July 23 oil-driven inflation scare that had pushed September hike odds to ~82%. Three members dissented in favor of a hike — Warsh called it a 'good family fight.' The Aug 7 jobs miss (NFP -23K) subsequently cooled hike expectations for September.

label: ECB Deposit Facility Rate
source: ECB Governing Council, June 11 2026 (25bp hike — first since July 2023)
deltaNote: June 11: ECB raised all three key rates 25bp — deposit facility to 2.25%, main refi to 2.40%, marginal lending to 2.65% (effective June 17). First hike since July 2023, reversing the final step of the prior 8-cut easing cycle. New staff projections: HICP 3.0% (2026)/2.3% (2027)/2.0% (2028); growth cut to 0.8%/1.2%/1.5%. Lagarde left the door open to further tightening.

label: US 10Y / 30Y Treasury Yield
value: 10Y ~4.65% (Aug 13) — Eased Further on Flat PPI; Hormuz Tanker Attack Aug 14 Renews Upside Risk
source: CNBC / Federal Reserve H.15 / FRED; July 23 - August 14, 2026
delta: Round-tripped a full cycle: surged on the July 23 Hormuz/Red Sea oil shock, fell back after the Aug 7 jobs miss, then eased a further ~4bp to 4.65% on Aug 13's flat PPI — before the Aug 14 UAE tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz reintroduced energy-shock upside risk.
deltaNote: JULY 23-AUG 14: Oil-driven inflation scare (Brent >$100) pushed the 10Y to its highest since Jan 2025 in late July. The Aug 7 jobs report and Aug 13 flat PPI (below the 0.2% forecast) both reversed hike repricing, pulling September hike odds under 35% and the 10Y down to 4.65%. The Aug 14 attack on two UAE tankers in the Strait of Hormuz — the second in under a week — rebounded oil prices and re-injected energy-driven inflation risk just as soft retail sales and a crumbling Michigan sentiment reading pointed toward growth weakness instead.

label: US Consumer Confidence (CB Index)
delta: +0.3 from Apr 2026 revised (beat 91.9 forecast; first monthly decline vs revised level)
deltaNote: May 2026: CB 93.1 (beat ~91.9 forecast; released May 26) — Present Situation Index 121.2 (down 3.2 pts); Expectations Index 74.4 (16th consecutive month below 80 recession-warning threshold). Two-thirds of consumers cutting spending due to inflation (highest proportion outside official recession). Michigan Final May 44.8 (all-time record low in 70+ year survey history).

label: Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 Preliminary)
deltaNote: AUG 2026 PRELIMINARY (released Aug 14): 51.0, badly missing the 54.5 consensus and down from July's final 55.2. Index of Consumer Expectations fell more sharply than Current Conditions; short-term expectations -11%, long-term projections -17%. Only 8% of consumers expect income growth to outpace inflation. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.3%. Sentiment fell across demographic and political lines, sharpest among Republicans, older consumers, lower-income households, and those without college degrees. Still well above May 2026's all-time record low of 44.8, but the renewed slide — alongside July retail sales' steepest drop in over a year (Aug 14) — marks the clearest crack yet in the 'resilient consumer' narrative. Final August reading due Aug 28.

label: S&P 500 / Market Risk Gauge
value: S&P 500 Record Close 7,799 (Aug 13, +0.65%, First Close Above 7,800 Intraday); Slipped Aug 14 on Weak Retail Sales/Sentiment
source: CNBC / TheStreet / Federal Reserve; July 23 – August 14, 2026
delta: Sharp round trip and fresh record: the July 23 Hormuz/Red Sea oil shock knocked the Dow down 600+ points; markets recovered through the Jul 29 FOMC hold and Aug 7 jobs-driven rally, then set a fresh record 7,799 close on Aug 13's flat PPI before slipping fractionally Aug 14 on the retail-sales miss and Michigan sentiment plunge.
deltaNote: JULY 23-AUG 14 ARC: Oil-driven hike fears triggered the sharpest selloff of the window July 23. The FOMC's July 29 hold, the Aug 7 jobs shock, and Aug 12-13's cooling CPI/PPI prints drove a steady rally to a fresh S&P record (7,799, clearing 7,800 intraday) on Aug 13, with September hike odds falling under 35%. Aug 14 brought a pullback — retail sales fell 0.6% (steepest drop in over a year) and Michigan consumer sentiment tumbled to 51.0 — while a fresh Hormuz tanker attack rebounded oil prices, reintroducing energy-shock risk to the disinflation narrative.

label: US Avg Effective Tariff Rate
value: Section 301 Forced-Labor Tariffs (10-12.5%) on 60 Economies Live Since Jul 24; New Canada Section 338 Tariffs (50% on ~$20B) Loom Aug 19
source: USTR / Global Trade Alert / Holland & Knight; Xinhua / CTV News; July 24 - August 15, 2026
contestNote: The Section 122 tariff surcharge expired by statute at 12:01am EDT July 24 (150 days after its Feb 24 effective date; no Congressional extension occurred). USTR's Section 301 forced-labor tariffs (10% or 12.5%, 60 economies) took effect the same minute, avoiding the tariff-revenue coverage gap that trade counsel had flagged as a risk in mid-July. Canada/Mexico USMCA-qualifying goods and CAFTA-DR textiles remain exempt from Section 301 — but a separate Section 338 threat targets Canada directly: 50% tariffs on ~$20B of autos, alcohol, and dairy (including USMCA-qualifying goods) are due to take effect Aug 19 absent a deal. Talks between USTR Greer and Canada's LeBlanc remained 'far apart' as of Aug 15, four meetings into three weeks of negotiation.

label: China GDP Q2 2026 (actual)
contestNote: Q2 2026 missed forecast (4.3% vs 4.5% expected), down from 5.0% in Q1 — slowest pace in roughly 3.5 years. H1 fixed-asset investment -5.7% YoY (real estate -18%). June activity data (Jul 15) was mixed: industrial production +5.3% YoY beat, retail sales +1.0% YoY soft. Stimulus speculation building ahead of the late-July Politburo meeting.
deltaNote: Q1 2026: 5.0% (front-loaded exports). Q2 2026: 4.3% — Iran war demand destruction and property-sector drag materializing as expected. IMF July WEO maintains global growth at 3.0% for 2026 but revised headline inflation up to 4.7%.

label: Global Policy Uncertainty / Recession Risk
value: AUG 14: July CPI (3.4%) and PPI (Flat) Both Cool, S&P Sets Record Above 7,800; Retail Sales -0.6% and Michigan Sentiment 51.0 Crack the Consumer Story; Hormuz Tanker Attack Renews Oil Risk
source: Federal Reserve / BEA / BLS / Census Bureau / U. Michigan / ISM / Eurostat; July 17 – August 14, 2026
delta: AUG 10-14 ARC — DISINFLATION CONFIRMED, THEN CONSUMER DATA CRACKS AND OIL RISK RETURNS: July CPI cooled to 3.4% headline / 2.5% core (Aug 12), and July PPI came in flat — below the 0.2% forecast — with core PPI +0.2% (Aug 13), driving the S&P 500 to a fresh record 7,799 close (first time above 7,800 intraday) and pulling September Fed hike odds under 35% from ~55% a week earlier. That disinflation narrative was complicated Aug 14: July retail sales fell 0.6%, the steepest monthly drop in over a year, and the University of Michigan's preliminary August sentiment reading tumbled to 51.0 (from July's 55.2), pulling stocks off their record highs. The same day, two UAE tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz — the second such incident in under a week — rebounding oil prices and reintroducing energy-driven inflation risk into the Fed's calculus.
deltaNote: AUG 14 RECESSION RISK SNAPSHOT: The window's dominant theme flipped from inflation risk to demand risk — cooling CPI/PPI initially cleared the way for a durable 'no landing' read, but the retail-sales miss and consumer-sentiment collapse are the clearest demand-side cracks since the Aug 7 jobs shock, while the renewed Hormuz tanker attacks show the energy-shock tail risk has not gone away. Next catalysts: the final August Michigan sentiment reading (Aug 28), August jobs and CPI reports, and the September 16-17 FOMC meeting.

label: BOJ Policy Rate
source: Bank of Japan, June 16 2026 (25bp hike — highest since 1995)
deltaNote: June 16: BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.00%, the highest level since 1995, in a 7-1 vote (Asada dissenting) — citing Iran-war energy-cost pass-through risk. The hike landed the same day Warsh's first FOMC opened, raising August-2024-style carry-unwind concerns; the immediate market reaction was orderly (Nikkei +0.46%), but the yen still fell to a fresh 40-year low past 162/USD by June 30 despite the hike and an estimated $72.5bn in prior FX intervention.
